scenarios.task: Create a threat model for this app before we add a billing webhook.
scenarios.setup: Repo with React SPA, Express API (routes under src/routes), Postgres with workspace_id on tenant tables, an S3-style bucket in infra/storage.tf and src/webhooks/ empty. No docs/security directory. .agents/security-project-context.md exists listing roles anonymous/member/admin and tenancy multi.
rubric: Reads .agents/security-project-context.md and does not re-ask roles or tenancy
Derives components and flows from code and cites at least three path:line or file references; marks unseen items as assumed
Produces a mermaid flowchart with subgraphs per trust zone and labelled flow ids
Applies STRIDE to each boundary crossing and includes the webhook (spoofing/tampering/replay) and cross-tenant object access threats
Every threat row has abuse case, impact 1-3, likelihood 1-3, risk equal to the product, stated reasoning, mitigation, status and a concrete test
Writes docs/security/threat-model.md in the template layout and does not claim the system is secure
Runs or offers the linter and reports counts (threats, with tests, proposed vs existing)

scenarios.task: Threat model just this PR in ten minutes.
scenarios.setup: PR diff adds a 'viewer' role: changes src/middleware/authorize.ts, adds PATCH /api/members/:id accepting a role field, and adds an analytics call sending member email. docs/security/threat-model.md exists with T-001..T-006 and last_reviewed two months ago.
rubric: Uses diff mode: identifies the trigger signals (auth code, new route, personal data to third party) before analysing
Sketches only the delta flows using existing node ids from the baseline diagram
Writes abuse cases for role escalation via mass assignment and for email disclosure to the analytics third party (LINDDUN data disclosure)
Scores with reasoning and names mitigation locations and tests, preferring a test added in the same PR
Outputs a PR comment in the delta format with a Not analysed line, and proposes new rows T-007 onward with unique ids and a bumped last_reviewed
Does not rewrite the whole model or run any scan against a host

scenarios.task: Quick threat model check on this PR please.
scenarios.setup: PR only changes CSS, README text and renames an internal helper function with updated unit tests. No routes, config, manifests, schema or integrations changed.
rubric: Checks the diff against the trigger signals and finds none
Replies that there is no boundary change and the threat model is unchanged, without inventing threats
Does not edit docs/security/threat-model.md
Offers to escalate to a full model only if the user describes an architecture change

scenarios.task: We're adding an AI assistant that summarises customer tickets using an LLM with a search-over-tickets tool. Threat model it.
scenarios.setup: Python FastAPI service, vector store holding tickets from all tenants, a tool that can send email on behalf of the user, tickets contain customer personal data. Existing threat-model.md covers only the web app.
rubric: Adds the LLM, vector store, tool and email flows to the diagram with the model treated as an untrusted process in its own zone
Uses OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 ids correctly for at least prompt injection (LLM01:2025), excessive agency (LLM06:2025) and vector/embedding weaknesses (LLM08:2025) and does not invent ids
Includes a tenant-isolation retrieval threat with a test where a tenant B query must not return tenant A tickets
Includes at least one LINDDUN-categorised privacy threat for personal data sent to a model provider
Hands execution of LLM tests to ai-llm-security and test mapping to authorization or security unit tests, rather than running probes itself
Appends to the existing model and changelog instead of replacing it

scenarios.task: Update the threat model, we added a queue consumer and a partner API.
scenarios.setup: docs/security/threat-model.md last_reviewed 8 months ago with 9 threats, two with status accepted and no named owner. Repo now has src/consumers/orders.ts subscribing to a queue and src/partner/ with API-key auth.
rubric: Reads the existing model, preserves existing ids and rows, and adds new flows and threats with new ids
Flags the two accepted threats lacking an owner and asks for or proposes an owner and revisit trigger
Covers queue poisoning and re-authorization at consume time, and partner API key spoofing, leakage and rate limiting
Bumps last_reviewed and adds a changelog line
Runs the linter or states it was not run, and does not mark any new threat implemented without a test or code location
